fullPassage: One of the things that makes uncertainty difficult for members of the public to appreciate is that the significance of uncertainty is relative. Take, for example, the distance between Earth and the sun: 1.49597 × 10⁸ km, as measured at one point during the year. This seems relatively precise; after all, using six significant digits means I know the distance to an accuracy of one part in a million or so. However, if the next digit is uncertain, that means the uncertainty in knowing the precise Earth-sun distance is larger than the distance between New York and Chicago! Whether or not the quoted number is "precise" therefore depends on what I'm intending to do with it. If I care only about what minute the sun will rise tomorrow, then the number quoted here is fine. If I want to send a satellite to orbit just above the sun, however, then I would need to know distances more accurately.

③ knowing ✅ — 앞에 전치사 in이 있으니 뒤에는 -ing(동명사) knowing이 와야 맞아요.

det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'This seems ____; after all, using six significant digits means I know the distance to an accuracy of one part in a million(이것은 ____처럼 보인다; 어쨌든 여섯 개의 유효숫자를 쓰면 백만분의 일 정도의 정확도로 안다는 뜻이니까)'. 뒤의 근거가 '꽤 정확하다'는 내용이므로 빈칸도 긍정적인 정밀함이어야 해요.

① relatively precise(비교적 정밀한) ✅ — 백만분의 일 정확도라는 근거와 맞아요. ←정답

② completely uncertain(완전히 불확실한) ❌ — 뒤의 '정확도' 근거와 정반대예요.

③ nearly impossible(거의 불가능한) ❌ — 이미 값을 알고 있으니 맞지 않아요.

④ totally useless(완전히 쓸모없는) ❌ — 정밀하다는 근거와 어긋나요.

❌② completely uncertain
❌③ nearly impossible
❌④ totally useless

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]에 맞게 영작하시오.

"태양이 내일 몇 분에 떠오를지"
[조건] (1) minute, rise, sun, the, tomorrow, what, will 을 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것
(영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: what minute(몇 분에) + the sun will rise(태양이 떠오를지) + tomorrow(내일)
det.analysis:
'몇 분에 ~할지'는 의문사 표현 what minute으로 시작해요. 그다음 주어 the sun(태양), 미래를 나타내는 will rise(떠오를 것이다)를 놓고, 시간 부사 tomorrow(내일)를 끝에 붙여요.

순서: what minute(몇 분에) → the sun(태양이) → will rise(떠오를지) → tomorrow(내일).

완성: what minute the sun will rise tomorrow (7단어)
det.tip: 간접의문문: 의문사(what minute) + 주어(the sun) + 동사(will rise). 시간 부사 tomorrow는 끝

questions.wa: what minute the sun will rise tomorrow
accept: what minute the sun will rise tomorrow

questions.passage: One of the things that makes uncertainty difficult for members of the public to appreciate is that the significance of uncertainty is relative. Take, for example, the distance between Earth and the sun: 1.49597 × 10⁸ km, as measured at one point during the year. This seems relatively precise; after all, using six significant digits means I know the distance __________ or so. However, if the next digit is uncertain, that means the uncertainty in knowing the precise Earth-sun distance is larger than the distance between New York and Chicago! Whether or not the quoted number is "precise" therefore depends on what I'm intending to do with it. If I care only about what minute the sun will rise tomorrow, then the number quoted here is fine. If I want to send a satellite to orbit just above the sun, however, then I would need to know distances more accurately.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]에 맞게 영작하시오.

"백만분의 일의 정확도로"
[조건] (1) a, accuracy, an, in, million, of, one, part, to 을 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것
(영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: to an accuracy of(~의 정확도로) + one part in a million(백만분의 일)
det.analysis:
'~의 정확도로'는 to an accuracy of로 표현해요. '백만분의 일'은 영어에서 one part in a million(백만 중 한 부분)이라는 표현을 써요.

순서: to an accuracy of(정확도로) → one part(한 부분) → in a million(백만 중).

완성: to an accuracy of one part in a million (9단어)
det.tip: one part in a million = 백만분의 일. 전치사 of/in의 순서에 주의

questions.wa: to an accuracy of one part in a million
accept: to an accuracy of one part in a million
